newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-ENGLAND UNHAPPY AT BUILD UP TO AUSTRALIAN MATCH.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-ENGLAND UNHAPPY AT BUILD UP TO AUSTRALIAN MATCH.

text.p: England captain Phil de Glanville said on Thursday the timing of Saturday's one-off test against Australia "heavily stacked" the odds against his team.
De Glanville said England had handed the Wallabies a massive advantage by agreeing to play the match just a week after the completion of the British Lions tour of South Africa.

At least 20 English players were involved in the Lions' triumphant campaign, but several, including Lions' captain Martin Johnson, elected not to come to Australia because of niggling injuries while those who did come have complained of fatigue.
"The jet-lag has really kicked in and there's obviously a lot of players that are really looking forward to a break," de Glanville told a news conference.
"I wouldn't say it's unfair ...(but) this is definitely going to be one of the hardest challenges we've ever faced."

De Glanville, who did not make the Lions' team, said England's preparation for Saturday's game had been less than satisfactory and added he would recommend that similar build-ups be avoided in future.
"I understand that it's in internationals that rugby makes its money but I think they (administrators) should try and give us every chance to beat whoever we're playing," De Glanville said.
"We want the odds stacked in our favour and this is not the case this time."
Saturday's test is part of a new agreement between England and Australia to host each other for one-off tests each year after just two meetings in the past nine years.
The last time the two countries met was at the 1995 World Cup when Rob Andrew's last-minute drop goal gave England victory.
Prior to that, their previous meeting was in the final of the 1991 World Cup won by Australia.
"We won the last game we played but I don't think that gives us any psychological edge," said de Glanville. "The teams are completely different now."
Australia's build-up to Saturday's test consisted of a series win over Five Nations champions France and a 30-13 defeat against New Zealand last weekend.
"I don't think the loss to New Zealand helped us," said de Glanville.
"We know they'll come out strong. Their national pride has been burt and they'll be doing everything they can to rectify it."

England - 15-Tim Stimpson; 14-John Bentley, 13-Phil de Glanville (captain), 12-Nick Greenstock, 11-Tony Underwood; 10-Mike Catt, 9-Matthew Dawson; 8-Tim Rodber, 7-Richard Hill, 6-Lawrence Dallaglio, 5-Simon Shaw, 4-Nigel Redman, 3-Darren Garforth, 2-Mark Regan, 1-Graham Rowntree.

Australia - 15-Matthew Burke; 14-Joe Roff, 13-Jason Little, 12-James Holbeck, 11-Ben Tune; 10-Tim Horan, 9-George Gregan; 8-Troy Coker, 7-Brett Robinson, 6-Daniel Manu, 5-John Eales (captain), 4-Garrick Morgan, 3-Cameron Blades, 2-Michael Foley, 1-Ewen McKenzie.
